title: Guarded Canary Runner Start Executor Implementation Result
claim: FP-MCP-318 was implemented in the MCP bridge by extending forgepilot_apply_guarded_canary_next_gate to support the sequencer-selected final runner-start attempt stage through the existing startRemoteRunnerRequest contract, while preserving the narrowed guarded surface.
summary: The MCP bridge implementation on branch feature/oauth-auth0 added dependency injection for the existing startRemoteRunnerRequest handler and a guarded executor branch for the sequencer state FRESH_ORIENTATION_BEFORE_START when the follow-on is forgepilot_start_remote_runner_request. With applyPreviewFollowOn=false it returns a preview-only runner-start boundary. With applyPreviewFollowOn=true it invokes the registered start handler once with START_REMOTE_RUNNER_REQUEST and reports a RUNNER_START_ATTEMPT boundary derived from the existing start result. The implementation reuses the existing server-side runner-start gates instead of reimplementing runner contact logic in the executor.
caveats: The running MCP service must be restarted before the rebuilt dist output becomes live.
This implementation result records code and verification only; it does not perform a runner-start test.
A live FP-MCP-318 functional test requires fresh approval, fresh clearance, fresh scoped enablement, and fresh runner capability observation.
The final live test may contact the runner start endpoint by design; that must be explicitly authorized in the test approval and must remain one bounded attempt.
boundaries: No runner start endpoint was contacted during implementation.
No approval was consumed during implementation.
OpenCode was not started during implementation.
The canary did not run during implementation.
Direct forgepilot_start_remote_runner_request remains hidden from the default narrowed guarded surface; the final start path is routed through forgepilot_apply_guarded_canary_next_gate.
